source_title: Nooka Ratnam et al. (2005). Check dam positioning by prioritization of micro-watersheds using SYI model and morphometric analysis — Remote sensing and GIS perspective. Journal of the Indian Society of Remote Sensing.
coverage: Targeted source-purpose screening and relevant passage accounting; not exhaustive main-paper extraction or source sweep.

identity.note: Historical IDs are preserved; citation and artifact title are trust anchors.

targeting_gate.verbatim_anchor:
After conducting intensive field visits, under- 
standing the soils properties, and also the quantity 
and velocity of run-off water, suitable sites for 
check dam construction were identified and marked 
(Fig. 7).
targeting_gate.rationale: Explicit GIS catchment priority plus field-verified check-dam positioning. Preserve both stages; do not recode erosion-need weights as structural suitability.

key_findings: Opening title/citation matches Nooka Ratnam2005 despite historical khan_maharjan ID.
Table1 PDF7 visually checked:13 land-cover weights,9 soil weight/delivery rows,6 slope classes. All are erosion/SYI inputs.
Tables3–5 show watershed results/ranks; not establishment thresholds. Table2 PDF9 formula OCR needs visual verification before reuse.
holds: Siting paragraph lacks thresholds/directions; runoff quantity/velocity ontology unresolved.
Erosion priority thresholds and weights cannot define T4 envelope.
Proposed-site stream orders are not a general suitability rule.

claims.quote:
The integrated study of SYI method is a very 
significant for prioritization of micro-watersheds. 
SYI model, which is an integration of the above 
discussed basin characteristics is used for 
automated demarcation of micro-watersheds for their 
priority. Valuable parameters considered in the 
present study are, (a) land use/land cover, a very 
significant primary map for an integrated approach, 
(b) soil, mainly purporting erosion study, and (c) 
slope a significant map for terrain study. Estimation 
of sediment yield is the main factor for study and 
development of the watershed, and it is useful for 
the automated demarcation for prioritization of 
watersheds, even without knowing of the rainfall 
data.
claims.note: Erosion-need prioritisation not establishment function. Table1 weights explicitly arbitrary on PDF7.

claims.note: Source-selected check-dam sites use field assessment after catchment prioritisation. Raw runoff quantity/velocity not identical to runoff-potential index; hold canonical mapping, family and calibration.

claims.quote:
Based on this study it is found that a 
total of 21 micro-watersheds fall under category very 
high, in which 24 check dams were proposed on 3rd, 
4 th and 5 th order streams.
claims.note: 24 proposed check dams in 21 high-priority micro-watersheds on orders3–5 is selected-site outcome, not universal order exclusion.
